summary: Comprehensive backend + frontend testing of Strayz educational adventure game. All 24 backend pytest tests passed (root, levels, puzzles 1-5, answer correct/incorrect/pattern/unknown, hint, player auto-create, progress with star-max logic, shop packs/purchase/invalid, AI riddle generation via Claude Sonnet 4.5 + answer validation). Frontend end-to-end flow verified: main menu (4 characters, 3 difficulties, 3 CTAs) -> story intro (6 dialogue steps, Skip/Next) -> world map (5 levels, levels 2-5 locked initially) -> /play/1 intro -> trivia + pattern puzzles render & submit -> hint deducts 15 coins -> Level Complete card with stars -> shop drawer (5 packs, purchase credits balance with +250 coins) -> Endless AI mode generates riddle, validates answer, shows explanation + Another One button.

issues: Character images appear visually duplicated: Max & Maya share the same yellow-hoodie portrait, Zoe & Leo share the same explorer-with-map portrait. Distinct portraits would improve family-character variety promised in the spec (ages 10/16/22/28).

action_items: (Optional/design) Provide 4 distinct character portrait images so Max, Zoe, Leo, Maya each look unique.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py uses deprecated FastAPI @app.on_event('shutdown') (works on FastAPI<0.110). Consider migrating to lifespan handlers for forward-compat.

_PUZZLE_CACHE is an in-memory list and AI-generated riddles are appended without bound; with many players generating endless riddles, memory will grow unbounded. Add LRU/expiry or store in Mongo with TTL.
/api/answer for pattern puzzles returns correct_answer as a comma-joined string while the client may need an array; current frontend handles it fine, but a list field would be cleaner.
Hint cost is hardcoded to 15 both in backend and frontend GamePlay; consider returning the actual deducted value and centralizing.

puzzles_data.py mixes trivia/riddle in one list; LEVEL 5 has 5 puzzles while levels 1-4 have 4 puzzles each — fine, but level intro shows '1/5' which is correct only because PATTERN_PUZZLES adds one more pattern puzzle per level. Total puzzles per level is consistent (5).
test_credentials: N/A - no auth in this app; player_id auto-created server-side and stored in localStorage on the client.
seed_data_creation: Test fixture creates TEST_player_<uuid> records and removes them via direct MongoDB cleanup after the session.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Full pytest suite is in /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py (24 tests). Endpoints all return JSON without Mongo _id leakage. AI riddle test creates puzzle, retrieves options, then submits each option until one matches - validates in-memory cache survives within the same request session. Frontend testids are well-distributed; primary ones used: main-menu-page, start-game-button, open-map-button, open-endless-button, character-card-{id}, difficulty-{id}, story-next-button, story-skip-button, level-card-{id}, play-level-{id}, locked-{id}, gameplay-page, level-intro, dismiss-intro-button, puzzle-card, trivia-option-{idx}, pattern-tile-{token}, hint-button, hint-shown, feedback-correct/wrong, next-puzzle-button, level-complete, nav-shop-button, shop-drawer, shop-pack-{id}, buy-pack-{id}, coin-balance, gem-balance, endless-page, generate-riddle-button, ai-puzzle-question, ai-feedback-correct/wrong, another-riddle-button, category-{id}. Note: lock testid pattern is `locked-{id}` (NOT `level-lock-{id}`).
